comment: The application -> CSS contract of the custom accent, the mirror image of runtime-contract.json's JS -> CSS one: an application writes ONE colour into --dx-accent-color, through themes.customAccentColor or by hand, and scss/widgets/fluent-next/_accent-color.scss derives the whole primary scale from it with relative colour syntax, by the same formula as the Blazor Fluent theme; the two copies are kept in sync by hand. These names are not part of the component tier - `accent` is neither a component nor a registered system concern - and fluent-next is the only theme that derives a palette, so tests/fluent-next-naming.test.ts excludes them from the public-surface checks. tests/accent-palette.test.ts holds the stylesheet, the generated palettes and the built bundles to this file.

input.name: --dx-accent-color
input.setBy: themes.customAccentColor(color), the documented entry point, or the application itself writing the property on the root element
input.acceptedForms: any colour the browser parses, including var(--custom-property) pointing at one; a value that resolves to no colour, or to another element's colour such as currentColor or inherit, is refused with W0024
input.whenUnset: every derived step is invalid at computed-value time, so each generated palette keeps the designed colour through var(--dx-accent-color-<step>, <designed value>)

base.name: --dx-accent-color-base
base.purpose: the accent normalized once: lightness clamped to 0.45-0.6 and pulled towards 0.525 as chroma falls under 0.02, so white, black and grays get exactly 0.525; alpha forced to 1. Every step is built from it, and step 100 is this normalized accent rather than the colour the application wrote

steps.alpha: the base ends in `/ 1`: relative colour syntax hands the alpha of the origin colour down, so an accent written with one would otherwise fade the whole scale; every step is built from the base and inherits its alpha
steps.fallback: the designed value of the step, so an unset accent leaves the theme exactly as drawn
